newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 17.

text.p: A Nihon Keizai Shimbun survey of 159 companies on shortages in corporate pension funds shows that about 40 percent of them would pump up pension funds within two years. A total of 14 companies will cover shortages in the year to March 1997, including TDK Corp, Obayashi Corp and Ajinomoto Co Inc. Those considering such measures number 18, including NEC Corp and Itochu Corp.

Ford Motor Co plans to buy nickel-metal hydride batteries to power electric vehicles (EV) from a joint venture formed by Toyota Motor Corp, Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd and other companies. Ford plans to sell EVs with the batteries from autumn 1998 in the United States.

Four of Japan's top six trading houses are not expected to meet their operating profit forecasts for the year to March 1997. The four companies are Mitsubishi Corp, Mitsui & Co Ltd, Itochu Corp and Marubeni Corp.
Mitsubishi Pencil Co Ltd is expected to see its parent current profits rise by 29 percent from a year earlier to three billion yen in the business year to December 1996, helped by the yen's weakness.

Toyota Motor Corp and Denso Corp plan to expand production sharing in ASEAN nations in an effort to take advantage of preferential tariffs of five percent or less under the ASEAN Industrial Cooperation (AICO) plan launched last month. Toyota plans to apply for the special AICO tariff by the end of this year.
